# Agent profiles

An AgentProfile describes what an agent is: its instructions, model, tools,
permissions, skills, and MCP servers. Put it in a file in your repository, and
every cloud agent you start from it behaves the same way, whichever credential
pays for the model.

## A profile in one file

Save this as agents/reviewer.json in your project:

```json
{
  "name": "reviewer",
  "description": "Reviews a change for bugs and missing tests.",
  "prompt": {
    "appendSystemPrompt": "You review code. Report bugs with file:line and a failing test for each. Do not edit files.",
    "instructions": ["Run the test suite before you report.", "Keep the report under 300 words."]
  }
}
```

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `prompt.appendSystemPrompt` | Text added to the harness's own system prompt. Use this for a role. |
| `prompt.systemPrompt` | Replaces the harness's system prompt entirely. Only harnesses with a real replacement control accept it; Claude Code does not. |
| `prompt.instructions` | Lines placed in the agent's project instructions. |
| `model` | Model hints: `default`, `small`, `provider`, `reasoningEffort`. |
| `permissions` | `allow`, `ask`, or `deny` per tool, keyed by the harness's tool names. |
| `tools` | Turn individual native tools on or off. |
| `mcp` | MCP servers: a local `command`, or a remote `url`. |
| `resources.skills` | Skills to install, inline or from GitHub. |

## Start an agent from the profile

The profile says what the agent is; the backend says which harness runs it and
how it pays for the model. Combine them in `create`:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { Sandbox } from "@tangle-network/sandbox";

const client = new Sandbox({
  apiKey: process.env.TANGLE_API_KEY!,
  baseUrl: "https://sandbox.tangle.tools",
});

const reviewer = JSON.parse(readFileSync("agents/reviewer.json", "utf8"));

const agent = await client.create({
  name: "pr-reviewer",
  backend: {
    type: "claude-code",
    model: {
      cliAuth: { account: "me", secretEnv: "CLAUDE_TOKEN", format: "token" },
    },
    profile: reviewer,
  },
  secrets: ["CLAUDE_TOKEN"],
  git: { url: "https://github.com/your-org/your-repo", ref: "my-branch" },
});
await agent.waitFor("running");
const review = await agent.prompt("Review the last commit.", { sessionId: "review" });
console.log(review.response);
```

Swap the backend and keep the profile: the same `reviewer.json` runs on
[Codex with your ChatGPT plan](/docs/cloud-agents/codex), on a
[coding plan](/docs/cloud-agents/coding-plans) through OpenCode, or on the
Tangle Router with no credential at all.

## From the CLI

```bash
# Validate a profile file
tangle agent profile validate agents/reviewer.json

# Show what's in a profile
tangle agent profile show agents/reviewer.json

# Start a sandbox with a profile file
tangle sandbox create --backend claude-code --profile agents/reviewer.json

# Or pipe it
cat agents/reviewer.json | tangle sandbox create --profile-stdin

# Send a turn under the profile
tangle agent prompt <sandbox-id> "Review the last commit." \
  --profile agents/reviewer.json --session review --stream
```

`--profile` also accepts an `https://` URL or a `github:owner/repo/path@ref`
reference, so a team can share one profile from a repository.

## From the platform profile catalog

The platform hosts a profile catalog with built-in profiles (shared, trusted,
versioned) and your own stored profiles. Reference one by name:

```bash
# A built-in profile from the catalog
tangle sandbox create --backend claude-code --profile code-reviewer

# Your own stored profile
tangle sandbox create --backend claude-code --profile my-custom-agent
```

The CLI resolves the name against `GET /v1/agent-profiles/:name` on the
platform, fetches the full profile, and installs it as the sandbox's backend
profile. You see built-ins plus your own profiles — never another user's.

## How profiles materialize

When a sandbox starts with a profile, the SDK:

1. Splits inline skills from the create request (keeping the POST small)
2. Primes the running sandbox with the full profile
3. The harness materializes skills into its native directory:
   - Claude Code → `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
   - Codex → `~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
   - OpenCode → `~/.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
4. MCP servers are configured for the harness's runtime

The agent doesn't read skill files from the prompt — the harness surfaces them
natively through its own skill-loading mechanism. The system prompt carries only
a lightweight index (name + description) so the model knows what exists.

## Several profiles, one sandbox

A sandbox can host many sessions, each with its own profile: a planner, a
coder, and a reviewer working in one checkout.

```ts
const planner = await box.agents.create({
  profile: plannerProfile,
  sessionId: "plan",
});
const builder = await box.agents.create({
  profile: builderProfile,
  sessionId: "build",
});
```

Each session materializes its own skills. When a session ends and a new one
starts with a different profile, the new profile's skills replace the old
ones in the harness's skill directory. The sandbox's filesystem (files the
agents wrote) persists across sessions.

## Snapshot provenance

Every snapshot carries a provenance receipt: which profile was materialized,
its content hash, and whether the profile changed mid-session.

```bash
# Snapshot includes provenance automatically
tangle sandbox snapshot <id> --name my-experiment

# Inspect the provenance
tangle sandbox get <id> --profile
# Agent profile provenance:
#   Base profile: gtm (a1b2c3d4e5f6...)
#   Effective:    gtm (a1b2c3d4e5f6...)
#   Materialized: 2026-10-14T22:00:00Z
```

If the profile changed mid-session (the agent modified its own configuration):
```
  Base profile: gtm (a1b2c3d4e5f6...)
  Effective:    gtm (f6e5d4c3b2a1...)
  Profile changed since creation (base != effective)
```

This answers "what configuration produced this state?" - the reproducibility,
auditing, and self-improvement primitive. The receipt enables:
- **Fast resume**: hash match skips re-materialization
- **Smart forking**: diff the effective profile against a desired one
- **Self-improvement**: correlate profile states with outcomes across runs
- **Auditing**: tamper-proof record of what ran

## Snapshot provenance

Every snapshot carries a provenance receipt: which profile was materialized,
its content hash, and whether the profile changed mid-session.

```bash
# Snapshot includes provenance automatically
tangle sandbox snapshot <id> --name my-experiment

# Inspect the provenance
tangle sandbox get <id> --profile
# Agent profile provenance:
#   Base profile: gtm (a1b2c3d4e5f6...)
#   Effective:    gtm (a1b2c3d4e5f6...)
#   Materialized: 2026-10-14T22:00:00Z
```

If the profile changed mid-session (the agent modified its own configuration):
```
  Base profile: gtm (a1b2c3d4e5f6...)
  Effective:    gtm (f6e5d4c3b2a1...)
  Profile changed since creation (base != effective)
```

This answers "what configuration produced this state?" - the reproducibility,
auditing, and self-improvement primitive. The receipt enables:
- **Fast resume**: hash match skips re-materialization
- **Smart forking**: diff the effective profile against a desired one
- **Self-improvement**: correlate profile states with outcomes across runs
- **Auditing**: tamper-proof record of what ran

## Profile lifecycle

| Event | What happens |
|---|---|
| Profile published | Stored in the platform catalog with a revision number |
| Sandbox created with a profile | Profile materializes into the sandbox; skills written to disk |
| Snapshot taken | The materialized skills are baked into the snapshot (reproducible) |
| Snapshot resumed | Skills are exactly as they were when snapshotted |
| Snapshot resumed with `--profile` | Workspace state from the snapshot, skills from the fresh profile |
| Profile updated | Existing sandboxes keep the old version; new sandboxes get the new one |

## From the SDK

```ts
// The profile rides the backend config
const agent = await client.create({
  backend: {
    type: "claude-code",
    profile: {
      name: "reviewer",
      prompt: { appendSystemPrompt: "You review code." },
      resources: {
        skills: [
          {
            kind: "inline",
            name: "review-checklist",
            content: "# Review Checklist\n\n- [ ] Tests pass\n- [ ] No new warnings\n- [ ] Docs updated",
            sha256: "...",
            byteLength: 72,
          },
        ],
      },
    },
  },
});
```

The SDK handles the wire-cap split (large skill corpora are deferred and primed
after the sandbox starts), so a profile with 30+ skills works out of the box.
